Vanessa — thanks for the ping. Notes for the packet:

- HSM models: We support Azure Dedicated HSM (HSM2-family), AWS CloudHSM (v4-compatible clusters), and on-prem integrations with SafeNet Luna 7. The attestation summary will list model families and minimum firmware levels we validate during onboarding.
- Key import/export: BYOK import is permitted only as wrapped key material; plaintext key export is not supported. We should explicitly state the constrained unwrap/export policy.
- Attestation flow: include the typical attestation steps (nonce challenge to HSM, attestation document signed by HSM vendor root, verification by Redwood key-mgmt service).
- Rotation: Our default rotation cadence is 90 days for customer-managed symmetric keys used for data encryption at rest; customers can set shorter cadences. Automatic rotation is supported for Redwood-managed keys with versioned key IDs.
- Emergency revoke: documented process and how it interacts with active tokens and running inferences (cache invalidation timeline).

I attached the latest KMS rotation policy excerpt. Also adding the TLS sample chain (self-contained PEM) — ensure the procurement team understands the sample is illustrative and we will supply production cert metadata in a secure channel.

Aditya
Sr. Security Engineer, Key Mgmt
Redwood Inference

David —

Thanks for the clear list. Responses below and next steps:

- Attestation signing cert fingerprint: The attestation verification chain uses vendor-signed attestation documents. For the attestation verification we validate the vendor intermediate signed by the HSM vendor root. The subject CN typically looks like: "HSM-ATTTESTATION-ROOT" (vendor-specific). We can provide the SHA256 fingerprint for the most common vendor roots we interact with (SafeNet Luna root, AWS CloudHSM root, Azure HSM root). Attached is a redacted table with the cert subjects and fingerprints.

- Rotation automation for wrapped BYOK keys: Wrapped BYOK keys are customer-owned and we do not automatically rotate the wrapped material on behalf of the customer. Customers may configure automated re-wrap flows using Redwood APIs or run manual rewraps; Redwood-managed keys (where Redwood holds the key material) are rotated automatically by our KMS on a configurable cadence. We will include a clear paragraph in the attestation letter stating this distinction.

- TLS versions/ciphers: Our platform supports TLS 1.3 by default. We also allow TLS 1.2 with a constrained cipher suite set for legacy integrations. Specifically we accept TLS1.2 with ECDHE_RSA_AES128_GCM_SHA256 and ECDHE_RSA_AES256_GCM_SHA384 when TLS1.3 cannot be negotiated. We'll include the exact cipher list and a sample server-side TLS configuration snippet.

- One-page attestation letter: Yes — we can generate a short signed attestation letter that summarizes the items above and references the attestation fingerprints. We'll deliver it as a PDF, and are fine providing the full artifacts under an NDA or through your secure file transfer.

Next steps: I'll attach the attestation-letter-draft and the fingerprint table to this thread. If procurement wants the full certs or manifests, I'll request an NDA and coordinate with Aditya for secure delivery.

Thanks — Vanessa
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
